This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

answer.answer: No. The historical accuracy rule (the old 2024 process that promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80) is no longer an alternative to the F1 gate. That legacy memo is explicitly marked as superseded and instructs not to apply the old rule. The current governing release policy requires promotion only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01 on a frozen holdout; a drift alert alone never authorizes promotion, and the previous production version is kept for rollback. So the accuracy rule has been superseded and is not a valid alternative to the F1 gate.
